check: Portable Objects through the Mac app's file dialogs (Export… and Import from File…) on the development Mac, driven through the Accessibility API: a document the iPhone simulator exported imports under its stable ID and exports byte-identical, reimports change nothing, and six hostile files are refused
limitations: Physical path for the Mac's file-dialog adapter only: the real app, AppKit's save and open panels, and the app's own container on the development Mac.
Driven through the Accessibility API by a test agent, not by a person. No pointer or keyboard event was posted.
No drag ran in this check: not between windows, and not to Finder, TextEdit, or another app. A person's drag has not been run. LAB-008-A's synthetic drag to Finder wrote no file.
A Debug build under a ticket-only bundle prefix, signed to run locally; not the installed app and not a Release build.
The other side of the round trip ran in the iOS simulator. No physical iPhone or iPad took part.

outcome.detail: Passed. S0 (682 bytes, SHA-256 4dfbd2a9…) reviewed “New to this lab” and imported as one committed Create Item receipt through the app UI, under the stable ID F1586771-0F15-4044-A372-5F9BC9968FDB. Export… saved “Glaze test · 釉薬 · crème · 🧪.anlab” (M1), 682 bytes, SHA-256 4dfbd2a9…, byte-identical to S0 and the bundled sample. S0 again, the bundled sample, and M1 each reviewed “Already in this lab”. The six hostile files were each refused with a sentence and no review opened: “The document is not valid JSON, so it was refused.”; “The document is larger than 2 MB, the most a lab object can be.”; “Attachment 1 has a path that points outside the object (it contains “..”), so the object was refused.”; “This object was saved in schema version 2 by a newer version of the lab; this version reads version 1.”; “This object carries a field that claims permissions or file access. Objects are data only, so it was refused.”; and “The document names the same field twice, so it was refused.” Each ended “Nothing was imported.” The simulator's re-export S1 reviewed “Already in this lab”, and a second Export… (M2) was byte-identical again. Afterwards the store held 12 demo items, 1 item of the person's own under the stable ID, and 3 committed app-UI receipts (the first-run Reset Demo, Create Collection, and Create Item), and every staging folder was empty.

steps: A Debug build of LabMac-Core with LAB_BUNDLE_PREFIX=org.example.lab008b, so the app ran in a container of its own, launched in the background with open -g
Before: a copy of that container's store held only the first-run demo seed: 12 demo items and 1 receipt
The app's NSNavLastRootDirectory preference pointed its file dialogs at a temporary folder outside the repository
Portable Objects: Import from File…, the simulator's first export (S0), Open; the review; Import
The object: Export…, then the save panel's Export with the suggested name (M1)
Import from File… with S0 again, Import Sample Object, and Import from File… with M1: each reviewed, then Close
Import from File… with each hostile file in turn: malformed, oversized, traversal-attachment, newer-schema, authority-field, duplicate-keys
After the simulator's second run: Import from File… with its export (S1), Close; Export… again (M2)
After: the store and the staging folders read from copies; the app stopped by its process ID
